description: The account filter blank on the SPACES route while the card filter is valid AND names a card that genuinely exists: the exact mirror of case07, and the folder's clearest proof that INPUT-ERROR short-circuits the read. 2200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS sets INPUT-OK, FLG-CARDFILTER-ISVALID and FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID at :610-612, then normalises: ACCTSIDI is eleven spaces so :615-616 matches on its SPACES disjunct and :617 moves LOW-VALUES into CC-ACCT-ID, while CARDSIDI is neither '*' nor SPACES at :622-623 so :626 moves the sixteen typed digits into CC-CARD-NUM. 2210-EDIT-ACCOUNT then sets FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK at :648, matches the not-supplied test at :651-653 on its LOW-VALUES disjunct, and sets INPUT-ERROR and FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK at :654-655; IF WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF at :656 still holds - its 88 value is SPACES at :135 and :264 set it - so :657 sets WS-PROMPT-FOR-ACCT and the twenty-seven characters of 'Account number not provided' reach WS-RETURN-MSG PIC X(75) and then ERRMSGO PIC X(80) through :494, twenty-seven significant characters followed by fifty-three spaces. :659 then moves ZEROES into CDEMO-ACCT-ID and :660 takes the GO TO, a forward early exit that becomes a plain Java return preserving evaluation order (rule R7), so the numeric edit at :665 is never reached on this path. 2220-EDIT-CARD then SUCCEEDS, which is the whole point of the case: it sets FLG-CARDFILTER-NOT-OK at :688, fails the not-supplied test at :691-693 on all three disjuncts - not LOW-VALUES, not SPACES, and CC-CARD-NUM-N is 923877193247330 rather than ZEROS - fails IS NOT NUMERIC at :706 because the value is sixteen digits, and so runs the ELSE at :716-718, moving CC-CARD-NUM-N into CDEMO-CARD-NUM and setting FLG-CARDFILTER-ISVALID. It writes NO message, so the single slot keeps 2210's text, and that survival is the mirror image of case06: there the account edit had already claimed the slot and the identical SET inside 2220 was skipped, while case07 has 2210 succeed silently so 2220's own text gets through. The cross-field edit at :637-640 needs FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK AND FLG-CARDFILTER-BLANK, and the card flag is ISVALID, so NO-SEARCH-CRITERIA-RECEIVED is never set: 'No input received' must not appear anywhere here, and neither must 'Card number not provided'. Those three texts are mutually exclusive by ordering alone, and cases 06, 07 and 08 together are what make the ordering provable (gate G30). Note also the asymmetry the two edits carry, preserved rather than tidied (practice B5): :676 moves CC-ACCT-ID, the alphanumeric X(11) view, whereas :717 moves CC-CARD-NUM-N, the numeric 9(16) REDEFINES over the same eleven- and sixteen-byte spans that app/cpy/CVCRD01Y.cpy declares, and this case drives the numeric side of that pair to a non-zero value (gate G34). INPUT-ERROR at :360 then sends the map and goes to COMMON-RETURN at :361-363, so 9000-READ-DATA is never reached - and the card chosen is deliberately one that is present, row index 2 of the seeded slice carrying card 0923877193247330, account 00000000002, embossed name 'Enrico Rosenbaum', expiry 2024-08-11 and status Y, so the READ at :742-750 would have answered DFHRESP(NORMAL) had it ever been attempted. That is what makes the short-circuit visible rather than merely asserted: a blank account buys the operator nothing even when the card beside it is real. Neither repository entry point is invoked - not CardRepository.readByCardNumber for the base key and not readByAccountIdViaAltIndex for the alternate one, since 9150-GETCARD-BYACCT is never performed from anywhere in the program and stays dead code (gate G45, practice B5) - and the non-invocation is asserted exactly where it is observable: CRDNAMEO stays at LOW-VALUES and does NOT carry 'Enrico Rosenbaum', which is precisely the leak this case guards against, while the three seeded rows are asserted byte for byte exactly as seeded with an empty write channel as the other half of that statement. 1200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS then paints asymmetrically: EIBCALEN is 172, so the ELSE arm runs; CDEMO-ACCT-ID was zeroed at :659 so :463 leaves ACCTSIDO at LOW-VALUES, while CDEMO-CARD-NUM is now 923877193247330 and therefore non-zero, so :471 echoes CC-CARD-NUM into CARDSIDO as '0923877193247330'; FOUND-CARDS-FOR-ACCOUNT is false because nothing was read, so CRDNAMEO, CRDSTCDO, EXPMONO and EXPYEARO stay as MOVE LOW-VALUES TO CCRDSLAO left them at :428 - binary zero, not spaces; and WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE at :490 still holds, so WS-PROMPT-FOR-INPUT puts the thirty-six-character 'Please enter Account and Card Number' into INFOMSGO PIC X(40). 1300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS is where this case earns its place. The turn does not arrive from the card list - CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET is 'COCRDSL' and CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM is 'COCRDSLC', so the conjunction at :505-506 is false - which sends both ACCTSIDA and CARDSIDA of the input group to DFHBMFSE and leaves the DFHDFCOL at :529-530 unwritten. The cursor EVALUATE at :515-524 is ordered, and arm one wins on the SECOND of its two conditions, FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK: :518 moves -1 into ACCTSIDL and CARDSIDL is never touched. That distinction is worth stating, because case05 reaches the same arm through FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK and the two conditions colour the field through different guards further down; the blankness itself arrives through the SPACES disjunct of :615-616, which is the disjunct a genuinely untyped field takes, rather than through the '*' marker a previous turn may have left in the same field. The colour guards then fire exactly once between them: :533 is false because the account flag is BLANK and not NOT-OK - the same one-byte field carries '0' for NOT-OK, '1' for ISVALID and a space for BLANK, and SET FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK at :655 replaced the NOT-OK :648 had set - :537 is false because the card flag is ISVALID, :547 is false for the same reason, and only :541-545 runs, moving '*' into ACCTSIDO and DFHRED into ACCTSIDC. So the screen leaves with ACCTSIDO showing an asterisk with DFHRED beside it and CARDSIDO showing '0923877193247330' with no asterisk and no red, and that one-sided outcome is the assertion. MOVE '*' at :543 space-fills its X(11) receiver rather than leaving the LOW-VALUES behind, because a one-character literal moved to an alphanumeric item pads on the right - so ACCTSIDO is an asterisk followed by ten spaces, not an asterisk followed by binary zeros; CARDSIDC is reported DFHDFCOL because 0x00 is that mnemonic on the colour plane and nothing ever wrote to it. COCRDSLC copies no CSSETATY - only COACTUPC does - and re-implements the highlight inline with the BLANK path gated on CDEMO-PGM-REENTER and the NOT-OK path ungated, so this case owns the gated blank side of gate G38 on the account field while the NOT-OK cases own the ungated one; flattening the two would silently stop colouring a rejected filter on first entry. INFOMSGC is DFHNEUTR from :556 because 1200 has already filled WS-INFO-MSG. 1400-SEND-SCREEN then moves LIT-THISMAPSET, which is PIC X(8) VALUE 'COCRDSL ', into CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET PIC X(7) - a PIC X receiver truncates on the right, so the surviving mapset is 'COCRDSL' - names CCRDSLA as the map, and sets CDEMO-PGM-REENTER, so the returned context is 1 again; :588 had already named COCRDSLC as CCARD-NEXT-PROG. COMMON-RETURN lays the 160-byte CARDDEMO-COMMAREA and the twelve-byte WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA into WS-COMMAREA and issues EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID('CCDL'), so every byte of conversation state travels in the payload and nothing is retained on the server (gate G37, rule R6). The commarea transition is deliberately observable: the account arrives as 00000000002 - the very account that owns the typed card, so the context could not have been more helpful - and leaves as eleven zeros, which is :659 taking effect; the card arrives and leaves as 0923877193247330, both because the URI names the record and because :717 writes the same value through the numeric REDEFINES view. The clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:16:00, the instant the source's own version footer carries, so CURDATEO and CURTIMEO are the literals 07/19/22 and 23:16:00 rather than today (practice B7), and the unit is reached as a plain Java object with the fixture-backed repository handed to its constructor - no MockMvc and no HTTP anywhere in the path (gate G51). CARDDAT is the only dataset seeded, because CARDAIX is a path over the same base cluster and not a dataset of its own (gate G45). Several gates have no site here: G32, because every GO TO in this program is a forward early exit or the shared COMMON-RETURN and there is no backward loop to restructure; G35, because there is no CALL 'CEE3ABD' anywhere in COCRDSLC, whose abend path is the CICS-native HANDLE ABEND at :250-252 into ABEND ABCODE('9999'); G39, because COCRDSL declares no PAGENO and no EXPDAY; G19 and G21, because no record is decoded on a path that never reads; and rule R4 with gates G22 to G28, because COCRDSLC holds no PIC 9(n)V(n) monetary field at all. The screen's four texts are pinned inside the send rather than in expectedMessages, because ParityCase reserves that list for lines a program emits through DISPLAY and COCRDSL's ERRMSG is PIC X(80) rather than the X(78) screen channel. The class is named CardSelectController because the migration plan names it so, while the source Function header, README.md:213-231 and CARDDEMO.CSD:220 DESCRIPTION(VIEW CARD DETAIL) all describe a card detail view - honoured verbatim per rule R1 and documented rather than corrected per practice B4, register AAP 0.8.4. No user rules govern this repository - review_rules returns exactly 'No user rules provided' - so the binding constraints on this fixture are the enterprise practices B1, B3, B4, B5, B7, B8, B11 and B12 rather than any project rule. Every expected value here was derived by structured reading of app/cbl/COCRDSLC.cbl against the app/cpy-bms/COCRDSL.CPY xxxI and xxxO PICTURE clauses, the app/cpy/CVACT02Y.cpy 150-byte record layout whose closing FILLER X(59) the seeded images carry, the app/cpy/CVCRD01Y.cpy REDEFINES pairs, the app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy title literals whose line 21 is commented out and line 22 active, app/bms/COCRDSL.bms and the real US-ASCII fixture whose row at index 2 genuinely carries card 0923877193247330 and the embossed name Enrico Rosenbaum; none of it was captured from a running COBOL program, because this environment cannot run one - eight blockers are recorded in AAP 0.7.6 and the substitution is escalated as risk R-A (practice B12).
